articles.title: I Paid $3,900 To Go on a ‘GLP-1 Vacation.’ Here’s What It Was Really Like
articles.summary: Woman attends a GLP-1 vacation at a resort on Hilton Head Island, South Carolina. Hotels are offering experiences for guests taking the weight-loss drugs.
articles.body: Teresa Barr recently took part in the “GLP-1 Support Experience” offered by Hilton Head Health on Hilton Head Island, South Carolina. The week-long program in a resort setting includes strength training workouts, cooking classes and mindful eating sessions for people taking the popular weight-loss drugs. It’s part of a trend of hotels offering GLP-1 vacations and adapting to guests’ new eating habits as more Americans take the medications. Barr, 63, of Rochelle, Texas, paid $3,900 for the Hilton Head experience and tells TODAY.com what it was like. I think I represent a lot of middle-aged women. I didn’t have a weight problem my whole married life. I had two kids, and I was able to bounce back to my original weight. I did not start having issues until I hit perimenopause and then eventually menopause, and then it was like slamming into a brick wall. I went from 113 pounds and ballooned to 165. I’m only 5-foot-3. I tried everything to lose weight, but wasn’t successful even though my lifestyle was healthy and I’m fairly active. Since taking the GLP-1 drug tirzepatide for the last 18 months, I have lost 25 pounds. I probably need to lose another 8 pounds to get my BMI in the normal range. I would then like to try to transition off the GLP-1 and keep the weight off. I came across a link to the Hilton Head Health experience on social media, and it checked all my boxes. I was like: I need more nutrition information. I definitely need a workout tailored for myself. If I could get some of those extra tricks and tools, I would be set up for success when I come off the GLP-1. I went for a week in November, and it reminded me of when I was in college. We were either in classes, cooking demos or in a lecture hall. The majority of my day was dedicated to the GLP-1 program — nutrition education and workouts with a fitness instructor. It was very busy. I started the day at 7:30 in the morning and didn’t get back to my room until around 6:30 or 7 at night. It was good — it was physically and mentally challenging. We had cooking demos taught by the chef. I love to cook, and I want to cook healthier recipes. It’s just learning that you can cook in healthy ways and it actually tastes good. There was a great variety of fitness classes. You had your traditional weight room with machines, dumbbells and kettlebells. Another classroom had the TRX suspension straps, which I hadn’t ever used before so that was cool. I had muscle loss the first several months of taking a GLP-1, so my big takeaway from the experience was that your protein needs are probably greater than you think they are. They show you what a high-protein breakfast and a high-protein lunch looks like, so that was helpful. I think I’ve been too complacent in the gym. You need to continue to build more muscle. So more repetitions and heavier weights are now a priority. I always struggled at my small hometown gym where there’s nobody showing you how to really do a good workout. Now, I have a workout program. I have some recipes I brought home and will be incorporating them into our family’s lifestyle. My big takeaway is that I’m going to be open, and I’m not going to beat myself up when I titrate down and go off the GLP-1. If for some reason I can’t maintain my weight and it starts to trend back up, I won’t hesitate to get back on a GLP-1 product because I’m not going back to those extra 50 pounds. That makes me very, very hopeful because I know the GLP-1s work, and they’re probably just going to keep getting better and better. I got to know many women at the Hilton Head experience, and I was very surprised the other ladies had been there before. They go every year. They go several times a year. They’re all going again next year. I would absolutely 1,000% go back. I would also like to take my grown, married daughters and let them experience what I did. articles.title: This Stress Hormone Can Raise Your Heart Disease Risk. How to Lower It Naturally
articles.summary: Cortisol is a stress hormone that can lead to high blood pressure and heart problems. A doctor shares a tip for lowering cortisol naturally.
articles.body: Cortisol doesn’t have a good reputation, especially when it comes to heart health. Many people know it as a stress hormone triggered by deadlines, life’s pressures, and conflicts at home and at work. You can’t live without cortisol, but you can keep it within normal levels and avoid prolonged spikes. Heart Health Tip of the Day: Manage Stress to Keep Cortisol Levels in Check Cortisol is the body’s most important stress hormone, said NBC News medical contributor Dr. Natalie Azar. It’s released by the adrenal glands, which sit on top of the kidneys. Short bursts of the hormone are important and necessary. Cortisol regulates blood pressure, among other things, and plays a role in the fight-or-flight response, she noted. “It’s essential for life. It’s not a villain, necessarily,” Azar said during a TODAY segment. “Cortisol is important in probably every single organ system you can name.” A little bit of cortisol gets people out of bed and makes them feel alert, said Dr. Taz Bhatia, an integrative medicine physician, on TODAY. But high cortisol levels due to chronic stress can lead to physical and psychological problems such as high blood pressure and inflammation, both doctors warned. So, managing stress levels is critical. Why It Matters Cortisol levels are naturally highest in the morning and lowest in the evening, Azar said. Levels of the hormone can also increase with stress from life events, work, relationships and finances, according to the American Heart Association. A study found that adults with normal blood pressure but high levels of stress hormones were more likely to develop hypertension and experience heart problems compared to people who had lower levels of the stress hormone. Cortisol can heighten cardiovascular disease risk, researchers warned in a separate paper. How to Get Started Combat high cortisol by reducing chronic stress with these evidence-based techniques: Take a deep breath: “Really take a minute to breathe” any time you get anxious, Bhatia advised. Try breathing exercises to ease stress.Exercise: The cortisol released from exercise can help you train your body to respond to cortisol in a “productive way,” according to Stanford Medicine. How you regulate your mind and body after a spurt of intentional physical activity is like a dress rehearsal for life’s tough moments. The next time a stressor comes up, you’ll have the tools to get your stress levels back to normal.Eat a healthy diet: Focus on nutrient-dense foods while avoiding processed foods and refined sugars.Get quality sleep: Not getting enough sleep increases late afternoon and early evening levels of cortisol, studies have found.Stay hydrated: Drink plenty of water and other healthy beverages for the heart.Laugh: There’s evidence that laughing can lower cortisol levels, Azar said, noting that if you force yourself to laugh or smile, it relaxes the nervous system. articles.title: Popular cruise ship rocked by illness outbreak as nearly 150 passengers and crew fall victim
articles.summary: With testing still pending, the CDC says nearly 150 people aboard Princess Cruises' Caribbean Princess reported vomiting and diarrhea on a 12-night voyage.
articles.body: A Caribbean cruise has taken an uncomfortable turn for nearly 150 passengers and crew members who have fallen sick with stomach illness symptoms — with an infectious disease expert providing important insight into a very "common" issue. A total of 148 people aboard Princess Cruises' Caribbean Princess — 134 passengers and 14 crew members — have reported the symptoms, according to the U.S. Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC). The ship departed Nov. 11 and is not scheduled to return until Nov. 23. It is carrying 2,936 passengers and 1,132 crew members, the CDC said. HIGHLY CONTAGIOUS NOROVIRUS SPREADS ON CRUISE SHIP, SICKENING OVER 100 PASSENGERS AND CREW Its 12-night round-trip voyage from Fort Lauderdale, Florida, includes scheduled stops in Aruba, Colombia, the Panama Canal, Costa Rica and Grand Cayman, according to the ship's itinerary. Princess Cruises reported the outbreak to the CDC's Vessel Sanitation Program (VSP) on Nov. 15. It also confirmed the situation in a statement to Fox News Digital. "Princess Cruises can confirm that a limited number of guests aboard Caribbean Princess have reported mild gastrointestinal illness," the company said in its statement. "Our crew responded promptly by implementing enhanced sanitation protocols across the ship, including comprehensive cleaning and disinfection measures." It concluded, "While most guests remain unaffected, we are continuing to closely monitor the situation." Test results are still pending, and the CDC said it is monitoring the ship's cleaning efforts and response. Those affected have experienced vomiting and diarrhea, though health officials have not yet determined what caused the illness. In response, the CDC said the cruise line and crew have taken several steps to limit the spread of illness on board. CRUISE BUFFET GUESTS FACE SURPRISE CHARGES FOR TAKING FOOD BACK TO CABINS Those steps include more frequent cleaning and disinfecting, keeping sick passengers and crew members away from others, and working with health officials on cleaning procedures and reporting cases. Crew members also collected stool samples from sick individuals to help identify the cause of the outbreak, the agency said. Test results are still pending, and the CDC said it is monitoring the ship's cleaning efforts and response. Fox News Digital reached out to the CDC for further details. Health officials say it can take time to figure out what is making people sick on a cruise ship. While norovirus is a common cause of stomach illnesses on cruise ships, the CDC said it is not always clear what is causing an outbreak when it's first reported. CLICK HERE FOR MORE LIFESTYLE STORIES The agency also noted that the 148 cases of illness were reported over the course of the trip so far — so not everyone became sick at the same time. To help prevent stomach illnesses, the CDC recommends washing hands often, especially after using the bathroom and before eating. ‘Very, very common’ "This is not the first time we've seen this with cruise ships," said Dr. Tyler Evans, an adult infectious diseases and addiction medicine physician who is also CEO, founder and chief medical officer for Wellness Equity Alliance in California. "Cruise ships, I often say, are sort of floating Petri dishes. They're these massive congregate facilities on the sea." CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR LIFESTYLE NEWSLETTER He said gastrointestinal illnesses on ships are "very, very common." A main reason is the food, he said — especially buffet set-ups, he noted. For anyone connected to this particular incident, he said individuals should look for "any sudden onset of vomiting and watery diarrhea. I know it's not glamorous to talk about," he added, "but if you are on the toilet more than five times a day, that is definitely an indication this is not normal and should be checked out by a primary care provider." Those with at-risk health conditions, particularly older adults, should be seen very promptly by doctors, he also said. Pregnant women as well as children need to be treated urgently as well, he said. Other cruise ships report similar illnesses The Caribbean Princess outbreak comes as other cruise ships have also reported similar illnesses this year. In March, 65 passengers and 11 crew members fell ill aboard Holland America's Westerdam during a February voyage in Asia, Fox News Digital previously reported. TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ Those affected reported diarrhea, vomiting and fever. Tests conducted by the ship's lab found that stool samples from seven patients were positive for norovirus. Health officials in Hong Kong boarded the ship on March 1 to investigate the outbreak. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP The cruise line said it increased cleaning and disinfection efforts, while authorities inspected the vessel before allowing new passengers and crew members to board. Jessica Mekles of Fox News Digital contributed reporting.

articles.title: Jax Taylor Was Diagnosed With Cancer Over the Summer After Waking up in ‘Horrible Pain’
articles.summary: Jax Taylor of “Vanderpump Rules” and “The Valley” reality TV fame revealed he was diagnosed with cancer over the summer after a tumor was found on his left kidney.
articles.body: Jax Taylor of “Vanderpump Rules” and “The Valley” reality TV fame revealed he was diagnosed with cancer over the summer after a tumor was found on his left kidney. “This is something I’ve kept private for the past few months because it’s been one of the scariest times of my life,” he wrote on Instagram Nov. 19. The 47-year-old said he woke up “in horrible pain” one morning in July and ended up in the hospital. “What I thought was just a kidney stone turned into something I never imagined. My CT scan also showed a tumor on my left kidney. After many tests and appointments I found out it was cancer,” he said. Taylor, whose father died from cancer, said learning about his diagnosis “broke” him. “It put me in a really dark place. The hardest part was the waiting. Knowing there was a tumor growing inside me while trying to go about my life like everything was fine. It’s crazy how you can act like everything is normal when deep down you’re a mess,” he wrote. Taylor said he underwent a five-hour surgery on Nov. 18 to remove the tumor, which was “a lot larger than they thought.” He’s currently waiting on the pathology results. Taylor shared several photos and videos of himself in the hospital, including one before and after his surgery. He also thanked his medical team and his girlfriend for standing by his side throughout his cancer journey. “I honestly don’t know how I would have gotten through everything without my amazing girlfriend by my side. She’s been my rock through all of this. She’s not just my partner, she’s my best friend and I feel so insanely lucky to have her in my life,” he wrote. Taylor was previously married to fellow “Vanderpump Rules” alum Brittany Cartwright from 2019 until she filed for divorce in 2024. They share a 5-year-old son, Cruz. Taylor ended his post with a reflection on his health. “If there’s one thing I hope people can take away from this, it’s never to take your health for granted. I did for many years and I won’t ever do that again,” he said. “Life can really change in a second. I’ve been given a lot to think about these past few years and if there’s one thing I know for sure it’s that nothing else matters more than your health your kids and the people that show up for you when it matters the most,” he added. In recent years, Taylor has been open about his health struggles. He said in his post Nov. 28 will mark his two-year sobriety anniversary. In 2024, the reality star said he had been diagnosed with bipolar disorder and PTSD. At the time, Taylor revealed that he had spent time in “an intensive inpatient treatment facility” “After many years of knowing something was wrong but not knowing exactly what it was, I recently learned that I was diagnosed with Bipolar Disorder and PTSD,” he wrote. Taylor acknowledged that the news was “a lot to process” but said he came home with a newfound “sense of peace.”

articles.title: The 2 Simple Exercises a Foot Doctor Does Every Day to Ease Pain and Swelling
articles.summary: A foot and ankle surgeon reveals the two things she does to keep swollen and achy feet feeling their best. Learn how to prevent the discomfort, too.
articles.body: The holiday season often means more time spent on your feet, from shopping, cooking and last-minute errands to traveling and more. At the same time, your leg veins, responsible for sending blood upward to the heart, are constantly working against gravity, and their health can affect your overall circulation, Dr. Ebonie Vincent, a foot and ankle surgeon, tells TODAY.com. Your age can affect your foot health, too: The fat pad that cushions the bottoms of your feet degrades as you get older, leading to soreness and stiffness. So, at the end of the long day, it’s no surprise your feet, ankles and legs may be aching and swollen. Luckily, Vincent has an easy, daily fix. Expert Tip of the Day: Elevate and Stretch Your Legs and Feet To Help Them Recover Considering all the work your legs and feet do, Vincent recommends elevating and stretching them for at least 15 minutes every day. Elevating them will address swelling, while stretching them will bring your muscles some much-needed relief. Why It Matters When you stand and walk for long periods, bodily fluids can pool and build up in the lower extremities. The subsequent swelling can make your shoes feel tight, make movement difficult and cause pain, according to the Cleveland Clinic. Depending on the shape of your shoes, the shape of your feet — especially if they’re flat — and whether you stand and walk all day long, you’ll likely experience pain in your arches, balls of your feet and your heels, too, says Vincent. This can lead to limited mobility, difficulty completing daily tasks and injuries that occur when you rely on other muscles and joints to make up for your foot pain. How to Get Started To address swelling, Vincent says to put your feet up at the end of the day for 15-30 minutes. Take off your shoes, and “elevate (your feet) above the level of your heart,” says Vincent. For example, you can lie down on your back and rest your feet on a stack of pillows. “That way you’re reversing gravity,” she adds, sending blood back up the body from your feet. For added relief, place an ice pack on your feet or lower legs. And if you want to address the swelling before you even get home, opt for wearing compression socks during the day, adds Vincent. She recommends those that with tightness range of 15-20 mmHg (millimeters of mercury) for moderate pressure. Next, to alleviate pain, stretch. “Stretching is very underrated,” says Vincent. “It’s amazing what you can accomplish with just stretching before and after activities. It’s free, and all you need to do is have time to do it.” Stand with both your palms out in front of you against a wall. While one foot remains flat on the floor, place the toes of your other foot against the wall while that heel rests on the ground. Lean forward until you feel the stretch in your calf. Then switch to the other side. To make the most of this stretch, Vincent says to remember the rule of threes: Complete the stretch three times per day (in the morning, the afternoon and the evening), do it three times in a row and hold the stretch for 30 seconds. articles.title: NHS Wales waiting lists grow for sixth month as longest waits fall
articles.summary: It comes as the number waiting for planned NHS treatment in Wales increases for the sixth month.
articles.body:
Wales' health minister has claimed that the Welsh NHS is in its strongest position heading into winter than ever before.

Mabon ap Gwynfor was speaking after the latest NHS performance figures showed that more than 11,500 people waited 12 hours or more in emergency departments from arrival until admission, transfer or discharge in one month.

The Welsh government's targets say no one should be waiting as long as this.

In September, there were 4,900 patient pathways waiting more than two years for planned treatment - a fall of 160 compared to the previous month.

But the overall number of people waiting for NHS treatment in Wales has risen for the sixth month in a row. In September, there were 721,400 waiting for planned treatment, compared to 714,200 in August.

'I spent more than two days waiting in A&E' - NHS bids to end corridor care

My 93-year-old mother waited 10 hours on the floor for an ambulance

With the longest waits falling slightly, ap Gwynfor said the figures were a sign that an investment of £145m earlier this year was starting to lead to improvements.

Earlier this week, Plaid Cymru ministers announced an extra £500m to cut waiting lists.

The latest figures on A&E performance showed that, in October, nearly two-thirds (61.1%) of patients spent less than four hours in emergency departments from arrival until admission, transfer or discharge. 11,830 patients waited 12 hours or more, though the way those figures are recorded has changed in recent weeks.

There was a decrease in the number of patient pathways when it comes to diagnostics, falling to just under 110,900, but an increase in the number of cases waiting for therapy, rising to just under 66,500.

Speaking to BBC Wales during a visit to Llandough Hospital on Thursday, ap Gwynfor said: "We are starting to see signs of improvement and it is encouraging we're on the right track, but we are yet to see the investment's full impact.

"The NHS is in a stronger position now than it's ever been in preparation for the winter."

But he warned of "impacts beyond our control", such as the El Niño climate phenomenon , or a flu pandemic, adding: "We are as prepared as can be, and I'm confident that the health boards have worked with us to develop the best plans."

"The situation as it is in emergency care in many departments across Wales isn't what it should be, and we need to fix that," ap Gwynfor added.

"We need to make sure that people don't wait too long, either in an ambulance, in an ED, or in a corridor, or waiting for discharge.

"That's why we've got a plan to increase and improve that flow to get people out."

Prof Jon Barry, director for Wales at the Royal College of Surgeons of England said it was "disappointing" to see waiting lists increase, "especially as we head towards the depths of winter".

"Thousands of patients are still waiting more than two years for treatment, many living with pain, restricted mobility and worsening health," he said.

"We welcome the £500m in additional funding for NHS Wales, including £25m to build and expand surgical hubs, announced in the draft Budget this week.

Reform UK Wales' Benjamin Hodge McKenna said Plaid was "settling for negligently" low waiting lists targets and highlighted that cancer performance had "plummeted for a second month running to just 57.1%, far below the 75% target".

"A competent government would deliver on both," he said.

Ken Skates, Welsh Labour spokesperson for health, said Plaid had "failed to get a grip on the challenges facing the NHS at precisely the time when resilience is needed most".

Natasha Asghar, from the Welsh Conservatives, said the figures showed the health service was "on its knees as waiting lists grow for a sixth month in a row".

articles.title: Dietitian Shares 2 Seasonal Sides Featuring High-Fiber Veggies
articles.summary: Hit your fiber goals with these dietitian-approved recipes for side dishes that feature healthy seasonal vegetables. They’re colorful, tasty and simple to make.
articles.body: Hitting your fiber goals is both easy and delicious when you lean on seasonal plant ingredients such as vegetables. “Research shows that eating enough fiber is necessary for good digestive and cardiovascular health, and fiber also helps keep you full in between meals,” Natalie Rizzo, registered dietitian and TODAY nutrition editor, said previously. Celebrate fall and winter flavors while supporting your heart and gut health with Rizzo’s tasty, nutritious side dishes. Maple-Roasted Squash With Pomegranate and Pecans For a dish that’s full of warm fall flavors, try Rizzo’s recipe for maple-roasted squash. She opted to use koginut squash, a hybrid of butternut and kabocha squashes, which has a tender and edible skin. A serving of this vibrant squash contains about 3 grams of gut-healthy fiber. If you’d prefer to use another squash, like delicata or butternut, you absolutely can. The pomegranate seed and pecan toppings for this dish add even more nutrients — especially fiber. With about 3 grams of fiber per serving, pecans are among the highest-fiber nuts out there. Crispy Green Beans With Shallot Breadcrumbs Roasted green beans are the star of this seasonal side, which then get topped with deliciously crunchy panko bread crumbs and thinly sliced shallots. Green beans don’t skimp on the fiber, either. Just a cup of cooked green beans nets you 4 grams of this gut-healthy nutrient. You could think of this as a lighter take on a classic green bean casserole, but this satisfying, nutritious dish deserves a place all its own. The trick is to layer the ingredients correctly during the cooking process so that they each take on the right texture to complement each other, Rizzo says.

articles.title: Letby prosecutors knew expert witness was under investigation
articles.summary: The Crown Prosecution Service knew an expert witness was being investigated by the General Medical Council.
articles.body:
Police and prosecutors knew an expert witness against Lucy Letby was under investigation over his fitness to practise when he gave evidence at her trial.

Prof Peter Hindmarsh testified that he believed that two babies Letby was accused of attempting to murder had been poisoned with insulin.

Before the first of his two court appearances, however, Hindmarsh had been referred to the General Medical Council (GMC).

The BBC has learned the Crown Prosecution Service (CPS) knew this before he went on to appear for a second time.

The CPS said it had "met all its disclosure obligations... and no objections were raised by the defence at any stage in relation to expert evidence".

Letby was convicted of murdering seven babies and attempting to murder seven others - one on two occasions - and sentenced to 15 whole-life prison sentences.

Prof Hindmarsh, who voluntarily removed himself from the GMC register before the investigation concluded, declined to comment to the BBC.

In November 2022, Prof Hindmarsh gave evidence to Letby's trial at Manchester Crown Court, telling the jury that the blood sugar of a child known as Child F fell worryingly low for a persistent length of time.

Skin injection would not fit with the 17 hours of hypoglycaemia the baby experienced, he said, as that would require repeated injections.

He said infusion would be "probably the most likely way of achieving the blood glucose effect that we have observed".

Giving evidence in February 2023, Hindmarsh told the court that poisoning was the only reasonable explanation for the blood readings of a baby, referred to as Child L, who was on the neonatal unit in early April 2016 at the Countess of Chester Hospital.

The court heard Child L's blood glucose levels remained low throughout 9, 10 and 11 April, even after an intravenous line and the connected bag containing the nutrients were replaced.

Jurors were told subsequent blood examinations found the baby boy's insulin level was at the very top of the scale the equipment was capable of measuring.

Hindmarsh, an expert in paediatric endocrinology at University College London at the time, agreed the readings could only be explained by "somebody having given insulin to [Child L]".

Shortly before this second appearance in court, the CPS had learned of the GMC investigation.

The BBC has not been able to verify the exact cause of his referral to the GMC, but the Guardian has reported it followed a complaint from Great Ormond Street Hospital, which, the newspaper said, had terminated his contract the year before.

According to guidance issued by the CPS in 2022, if information is received that "casts doubt on the competence and/or credibility of an expert witness... the disclosure implications need to be considered".

It adds "the methodology used by the expert may be discredited" and "such information may render past convictions unsafe".

The guidance adds: "In deciding whether action is needed in such cases, the overriding principle to be considered is public confidence in the integrity of the criminal justice system."

The BBC has asked the CPS whether it had any plans to refer the use of Hindmarsh as an expert witness in the Letby prosecution to its director of legal services.

The CPS said regulatory investigations were separate and independent of criminal proceedings, and the existence of an investigation did not determine whether evidence was admissible or reliable.

According to the Guardian, Letby's defence team, when initially told of the investigation into Hindmarsh, did not make an application to put the information before the jury because the CPS had said it would oppose it.

The opposition was said to be because the GMC had not reached a final conclusion.

The Guardian reported the CPS had seemingly not been told of a previous tribunal ruling and that Hindmarsh had been barred from treating patients.

The investigation into Hindmarsh never concluded because, according to GMC records, he "relinquished" his registration in November 2024 through a process known as "voluntary erasure".

The GMC has not responded to the BBC's request for comment.

articles.title: Yemen’s besieged city of Taiz faces a deepening water crisis
articles.summary: Fuel shortages and the loss of access to wells have left residents dependent on unsafe water.
articles.body:
Taiz, Yemen – Qaid al-Sharaabi waited three days before it was his turn to receive a tanker of clean water.

But the delay is not the only problem. He says he now has to pay more – the result of the Houthi siege on Taiz , in southwestern Yemen.

“This is the second time since the siege began a month-and-a-half ago that I’ve had to pay twice the price for a water tanker,” al-Sharaabi told Al Jazeera. “I’m afraid that if things continue like this, more residents will resort to using unsafe water.”

The United Nations children’s agency (UNICEF) says that water production in Taiz has nearly halved, while more than 800,000 people are reported to be cut off from humanitarian assistance.

The crisis has left the city reeling , even as government soldiers try to defend it, in the latest round of fighting to hit the area since the war in Yemen started in 2014.

Hospital administrators are warning of a public health disaster, while government officials are unsure how much longer they will have the funds needed to carry out even limited services.

Taiz, Yemen’s third-largest city, has long suffered from severe water shortages.

But, according to Wafiq al-Aghbari, director-general of Taiz governorate’s Local Water and Sanitation Corporation, the crisis “intensified in 2015, with the first siege imposed on the city by the Houthis, and continued to worsen year after year, as the suffering of the city’s residents grew”.

He said the crisis has deepened since the Houthis laid siege to the city again in October, after they made advances against government forces in the countryside around Taiz.

Before the war started in 2014, al-Aghbari explained, Taiz received about 20,000 cubic metres (700,000 cubic feet) of water per day from six large wellfields, which had supplied the city and its immediate surroundings for years.

But only one of those wellfields is inside the city limits, and before the war, it had only been used in emergencies.

By 2015, Taiz had lost access to all five of its external wellfields, which had either fallen under Houthi control or were on the front lines, leaving the city reliant on its emergency wells.

But work in the past few years to dig additional wells and rehabilitate existing sources had brought daily production capacity up to 5,000 cubic metres (175,000 cubic feet) – still just 14 percent of the city’s estimated daily needs.

The Houthi encirclement of Taiz in October led to the Iranian-backed group seizing control of Hadhran al-Dhabab, an external wellfield that had been partially restored in August 2025.

The situation has led to the water corporation losing 3,200 cubic metres (112,000 cubic feet) of daily production capacity – 1,200 cubic metres (42,000 cubic feet) after pumping stopped from the Hadhran al-Dhabab wellfield, and a further 2,000 cubic metres (70,000 cubic feet) after wells inside the city stopped operating because of a shortage of diesel. The corporation is now able to produce only 1,800 cubic metres (63,180 cubic feet) a day from the emergency wells that it can still operate.

Al-Aghbari said the consequences of the siege had extended beyond the widening gap between water supplies and demand.

Funding and supplies for the city’s charitable water distribution points, known as “sabeel”, have also been disrupted, because of shortages of fuel and water.

According to al-Aghbari, the subsidised distribution points had previously provided up to 1.5 million litres (396,000 gallons) of fresh water a day, alongside a further 1 million litres (264,000 gallons) of untreated water.

“The water corporation has entered a major financial crisis as a result of the loss of most international and local funding for its operations, at a time when the corporation is also under immense pressure because of the growing shortfall in meeting local water needs,” al-Aghbari said.

He added that this was especially problematic because more residents cannot afford to buy commercially-supplied water as a result of the worsening economic situation, and become more dependent on the free water distribution points.

The owner of one commercial water tanker, who did not want to give his name for security reasons, said that prices had risen sharply at the beginning of the siege, from 18,000 riyals per tanker (about $12 at parallel market rates) to 30,000 riyals (about $20).

He continues to try to pick up water from the Hadhran al-Dhabab wellfield, but said that the process had become difficult.

“[That is] because of the consequences of the siege, including the inspection procedures imposed by the Houthi group … which last for hours,” he said. “Sometimes we are prevented from entering and remain outside the city for more than a day, on the grounds that there are risks because of heightened military and security tensions.”

The Houthis have denied responsibility for the closure of roads into Taiz. Human Rights Watch has said that residents, aid workers, and UN officials had blamed the armed group for shortages in the city.

The consequences of the siege have gone beyond its humanitarian and economic impact, with serious implications for public health, according to Dr Abdulqawi al-Shamiri, the director of Taiz’s al-Taawun Hospital.

He warned of “serious health disasters because of the interruption of safe water supplies that residents used to obtain from groundwater fields outside the city”.

Al-Shamiri said water from the emergency wells within the city had “long been unfit for human use, as a large proportion of it has become contaminated, or is hard water containing high concentrations of salts”.

He explained that the contamination was the result of sewage mixing with water because of poorly maintained sewage networks, and rubbish dumped in streets and floodwater channels. The Houthis, al-Shamiri said, have prevented waste from being transported to a landfill outside the city.

According to an internal report from the governorate’s Cleaning and Improvement Fund, close to half of the city’s rubbish is going uncollected.

Residents are contracting illnesses such as cholera and acute diarrhoea as a result, Al-Shamiri said.

“The rubbish quickly decomposes into extremely dangerous bacteria and chemicals that increase the existing contamination of the city’s well water, making it unfit for human use,” al-Shamiri said. “Unfortunately, however, most people are being forced to use it under the current circumstances because of the difficulty of accessing clean, safe water.”

articles.title: 8 Exercises for Gamers To Prevent and Treat Wrist, Neck and Shoulder Pain
articles.summary: Playing the new “Grand Theft Auto?” experts recommend these streches and exercises to keep your back and neck feeling their best while you’re gaming.
articles.body: If your plans include an extended trip to Vice City this week, you probably expect your body to be hurting. But whether or not you’re a “Grand Theft Auto” fan, anyone who sits for long periods of time could probably use some pain relief. Sitting for long periods while gaming puts a strain on the body that’s similar to sitting for hours at a desk job or in your car, Mitchell Murphy, a certified trainer at Anytime Fitness in Woodbury, Minnesota, tells TODAY.com. “As a gamer myself, I know it’s (during) those prolonged periods of sitting that...we get sucked into our video games,” he says, “and with that comes a hunched-over position.” Physical therapist Austin Afshar also understands “the time suck” that gaming can lead to. Having found himself frequently playing previous installments in the “GTA” franchise until the early hours of the morning, he tells TODAY.com there is definitely the possibility for enthralled gamers to end up with aches, pains and stiffness. Sometimes it’s hard for people to understand how sitting for hours at a time could lead to an injury, says Afshar, who is also a certified strength and conditioning coach and Brooklyn regional director with Spear Physical Therapy. “Well, how do you feel when you sit in a car for two hours?” he says. If you think about it that way, it’s not so surprising that staying in one position on a couch or gaming chair could leave you feeling sore. But the trainers say it doesn’t have to be that way. How Gaming Causes Wrist, Neck, Shoulder and Hip Pain First, there are risks that come with “just being static,” Afshar says. “Think about holding a coffee mug out in front of you,” he says. “It feels light at first, but after a few minutes, you’d really probably like to put it down.” In this way, “A position can become tiring simply because you’ve held that for such a long time,” he explains. And poor posture only compounds the problem. If you’re holding yourself in a hunched over position, that can lead to something called upper crossed syndrome, which means the muscles in the front of your chest are consistently tight and “working over time” while the muscles in your upper back are “on vacation,” Murphy explains. A similar situation — colloquially termed “dead butt syndrome” — arises in your hips and glutes. Here, your glutes and hamstrings along the back of your legs are weakened while the quads in the front of your legs remain tight for hours at a time, as TODAY.com explained previously. In both situations, you might notice aches, pains, stiffness and even numbness resulting from these muscle imbalances. Over time, that can lead to reductions in your range of motion, Murphy notes. The repetitive motions of playing video games also put you at risk for injuries to the wrists, elbows and shoulders, Afshar says. This series of joints is called the upper body’s “kinetic chain.” You might notice irritation in the tendons, muscles or nerves in the form of pain on one side of your wrist when you’re gripping a controller or a twinge on your thumb while using the joystick, he says. You should take note of the first sign of pain or discomfort like this, Afshar says, especially if it starts to creep into other parts of your life (like trying to open a jar) or if you notice that irritation earlier and earlier in your gaming sessions. Fortunately, there are some simple ways to both prevent and manage these painful, irritating symptoms so you can get back to gaming. Best Exercises for Gamers to Prevent Pain Here are a few trainer-approved exercises to prevent common injuries to your wrists, neck, shoulders and back while playing video games for long periods. Get in the habit of performing a set of these before you pick up the controller, Afshar says. And when you take breaks, go ahead and do another set or two. Wrist Flexion and Extension For this simple stretch from Murphy, hold your arm out in front of you with your palm facing upward. With your other hand, grab your fingers and gently pull them towards your body to feel a forearm stretch. This is a wrist extension. Hold that for about 10 to 15 seconds and then relax. Then repeat for another two times. Then, flip your outstretched arm over so that your palm is facing down. Again, gently pull on your fingers to feel a feel a stretch in the top of your forearm through a wrist flexion. Again, hold the stretch for about 10 to 15 seconds, relax and then repeat. Wrist Mobility Stretch Afshar recommends this simple movement to support wrist mobility. To start, lay your forearm on the edge of a table so that your hand lies limp over the edge. From there, you’ll gently and slowly lift and lower your hand at the wrist, he says. Try that for each wrist for five to 10 reps. Wrist Side Sweeps Think of this movement like a windshield wiper with your hand, Afshar says. Place a forearm on a table, your bed or your knee with your palm flat on the surface. Then, bending at the wrist, move your hand towards your thumb and back in the direction of your pinky. Repeat that on each hand for a total of five to 10 repetitions. This one will “keep your wrist moving in a different direction,” Afshar says. Seated Ear-to-Shoulder Stretch This simple stretch will help ease tightness and soreness in your neck and shoulders. In a seated position, look forward and gently try to bring one ear down to your shoulder on that side. To make the stretch a little deeper, Murphy will place one the hand on his head and gently press down. He recommends holding that stretch for 10 to 15 seconds on either side and then repeating it for a total of two to three reps on each side. Neck Turns While your character in “GTA VI” is running and looking around, you’re staying static and staring forward at the screen, Afshar says. These simple neck turns will help combat that. To perform this stretch, keep your chest facing forward while you turn your head gently to look to one side. Then, slowly come back to center before turning to look to the other side. Hold the stretch for three to five seconds on each side. “Only go as far as feels comfortable. Don’t push it,” he says. Chin Tucks This is a small movement with big benefits. Sit up straight and imagine a microphone is just an inch too close to your mouth, Afshar says. “Keep your eyes level and gently slide your head straight back, almost like you’re making a double chin,” he advises. The exercise should feel small and easy. Hold the chin tuck for about five seconds and then return to your starting position. Repeat that five to 10 times. Upper Back Mobility Stretch If you’re feeling tightness in your upper back and neck area, Murphy recommends giving this mobility exercise a try. Start by interlacing your fingers and hooking them around the base of your head. Keep your elbows tucked inward, breathe out and gently pull down with your fingers to bring your head forward and down. Hold that for 10 to 15 seconds. For a little more mobility work, Murphy likes to move his chest in large, gentle circles while in this position. Scapular Squeezes For those who tend to hunch their shoulders while sitting, this small stretch will feel great. First, stand up straight with your arms by your sides. Then, imagine gently lowering your shoulders and squeezing your shoulder blades together. Hold that for five seconds and then release. “When you’re seated in that position, whether it’s driving, working or playing a game, you tend to like cave inwards,” Afshar says. “So you need to work on opening up at your chest to keep the shoulders back.” This exercise also helps with neck pain, he adds. Other Tips to Feel Good While Gaming Keep Posture in Mind For Murphy, good posture is top of mind while gaming. “If I’m in between missions or my character dies, I tell myself, ‘Okay, Mitchell, nice proud chest, let’s roll those shoulders back,’” he says. “That will help engage the core and bring those back muscles into play as well.” Afshar agrees that good posture is a must if you know you’re going to be gaming for hours at a time. “At minimum, you should be seated with your feet flat on the ground and sit up nice and tall,” he says. “Make sure you’re not leaning forward or leaning back.” Prepare Healthy Snacks and Drinks As important as regular movement is to prevent pain, you can also help your body keep feeling its best with smart food and drink choices, Murphy says. “It’s a lot easier said than done,” he acknowledges, especially when so many of us tend to pick at calorie-dense snacks while gaming or run to grab whatever’s convenient in the fridge. That’s why it’s helpful to have some nutritious options in mind ahead of time, Murphy says. In particular, he’s a fan of carbonated water rather than soda and will reach for baby carrots and beef jerky rather than chips. Take Regular Breaks And both experts note the unique risks of going from sitting in a car to sitting at work to sitting at home while playing “GTA VI.” That amounts to hours of holding the same sitting position over the course of a full day. The single best thing you can do to prevent pain is to simply “take a lap,” Afshar says. Just standing up, doing a few squats, and walking around your home or around the block every once in a while is surprisingly effective, he says. Ideally, gamers should try to take a break like this every 30 to 45 minutes, Afshar says. But you can also plan around certain cues such as completing a mission in the game, setting a timer on your phone or taking advantage of the natural need for bathroom breaks and water refills, Murphy adds. However, you should resist the urge to immediately pick up your phone. “What most people do nowadays is they put the controller down, but they pick up their phone, and it’s the same thumb (movement),” Afshar says. “That’s no better than just still playing.”

articles.title: Medical College Hospital counts its losses after Wednesday night violence on campus allegedly carried out by Akhil Bharatiya Vidyarthi Parishad supporters
articles.summary: Campus violence erupted at Kolkata’s Medical College Hospital after clashes over show-cause notices; interns injured, windows smashed, ABVP denies role.
articles.body: Kolkata: Broken window panes, scattered glass shards near the administrative building, and bruised medical interns—these were the scenes at Medical College Hospital (MCH), Kolkata, on Thursday morning as the institution took stock after a night of campus violence allegedly carried out by Akhil Bharatiya Vidyarthi Parishad (ABVP) supporters.On Wednesday evening, junior doctors and interns were staging a sit-in near the principal’s office on the ground floor of the administrative building. They were demanding the revocation of show-cause notices served on eight interns for holding a media briefing following the Chorbagan stampede.Tensions had already been high on College Street throughout the day, with SFI and ABVP members clashing over setting up a bookstall outside the University of Calcutta. Around 7.30pm, the violence spilled over onto the MCH campus when alleged ABVP members—some armed with lathis—entered through Gate 1 and attacked the protesting interns.The assailants allegedly smashed administrative building windows with stones and lathis, and assaulted interns who tried to resist. Junior doctors attempting to record the incident on their phones were also targeted; one sustained injuries to his back, while another was reportedly choked.“The attackers were outsiders; we have never seen them here. From the moment they entered the campus to when they reached the administrative building, the police stood by as mute spectators. We were beaten up right in front of them. When I tried to save my colleague from their clutches, they punched me,” recounted junior doctor Arnab Talukdar.The violence continued until 10pm. Junior doctors took shelter inside the administrative building and locked the gates, while patients’ relatives scrambled for cover. “I was sitting on a staircase opposite the emergency building when I saw groups of people barging in. Within moments, the campus turned into a battlefield, and I ran out onto the road for safety,” said a woman whose husband is undergoing treatment at the hospital.“They were trying to break the collapsible gate of the administrative building. When they saw me recording, they pounced on me to snatch my phone, throttled me, and shattered my glasses,” said second-year medical student Susanta Das.Even after the attackers left, students and doctors remained barricaded inside. According to students, police escorted Principal Indranil Biswas out of the building around 10.45 pm. The interns finally returned to their hostels after midnight. “Senior doctors and postgraduate trainees (PGTs) guarded us and helped us get back safely,” said third-year student Shibam Mondal.Responding to the incident, ABVP state secretary Nilkantha Bhattacharya denied the allegations and blamed Left student groups. “For a long time, certain Left organisations have been trying to create instability across colleges and universities in Bengal. What happened at MCH is deeply shameful and unacceptable, especially at a healthcare institution. A section of Left-aligned students surrounded the principal’s chamber and tried to break doors and windows by hurling stones and bricks.
